hero.headline: US strikes Iran for second time in three days during fragile ceasefire
hero.body:
The United States conducted military strikes against targets in Iran for the second time in three days, according to reports. The attacks targeted a drone launch site as hostilities continued during what has been described as a fragile ceasefire between the two nations.

The strikes come as the US and Iran remain engaged in negotiations aimed at ending a three-month war. President Trump has maintained what sources describe as maximum demands on Iran during the talks. The conflict has raised concerns about disruption to shipping in the strategically important Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil transit.

Oil markets responded to the renewed strikes, with prices jumping on fears that disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz could affect global supply. The waterway handles a significant portion of the world's petroleum shipments, making any military action in the region a concern for energy markets.

The strikes occurred despite ongoing diplomatic efforts to reach an accord between Washington and Tehran. According to multiple reports, no agreement appears imminent as Trump continues to hold firm on his negotiating position. The president has reportedly expressed indifference to political pressure related to the midterm elections as the military actions continue.

The three-month conflict represents one of the most significant direct military confrontations between the United States and Iran. Previous tensions between the nations had typically involved proxy forces or more limited engagements, making the current sustained hostilities notable in the history of US-Iran relations.

The timing of the strikes, occurring during ceasefire negotiations, highlights the precarious nature of the current diplomatic process. Military officials have not provided detailed information about the specific targets hit or the extent of damage caused by the latest round of strikes.

The situation remains fluid as both military operations and diplomatic talks continue simultaneously. The international community has expressed concern about the potential for the conflict to escalate further or to disrupt vital shipping lanes that serve as arteries for global commerce.

cards.headline: US conducts second round of strikes on Iran in three days
cards.body:
The United States carried out fresh military strikes against Iranian targets in southern Iran on Wednesday, representing the second offensive operation within three days as a ceasefire between the two nations remains fragile and peace negotiations continue.

According to US officials, the strikes were executed as a defensive measure in response to Iranian military activity. The attacks targeted four one-way attack drones and a drone ground-control station operated by Iranian forces at military sites in the region.

These operations risk destabilizing the currently tenuous ceasefire that has been holding between the two countries. Diplomatic efforts to resolve the three-month conflict remain ongoing, though military escalation threatens to undermine the negotiation process.

The strikes triggered immediate market reactions, with oil prices climbing sharply as investors grew concerned about potential disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most critical trade corridors for energy transport. Approximately 20 percent of global crude oil passes through this narrow waterway, making any threat to its security a significant economic concern.

When asked about the strikes, President Trump stated he faces no political pressure to reach an agreement with Iran ahead of midterm elections. He indicated a willingness to outlast Iranian negotiators in talks and suggested electoral considerations would not shape his approach to the conflict.

The three-month war has already caused substantial damage to regional infrastructure. Recent Iranian drone strikes hit Kuwait's oil sector, causing severe damage to petrochemical plants and other facilities. Similar attacks have struck targets in the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain. These incidents have contributed to what analysts describe as the largest disruption to oil supplies in history, with Brent crude prices rising significantly from earlier in the year.

The conflict has also had spillover effects in neighboring countries. In Lebanon, clashes between Israel and Hezbollah have intensified in the southern regions, leaving residents skeptical that US-Iran negotiations will ease violence affecting their territory.

Meanwhile, Iran has begun restoring internet access to its population following an 88-day near-total shutdown. The government has allowed some users to reconnect to services previously blocked, though access remains limited and uncertain. Many Iranians question how long the restored connectivity will persist.

The Pentagon characterized Wednesday's strikes as defensive responses to immediate threats from Iranian drone operations. Military officials have not announced plans for additional military action at this time, though the volatile situation demonstrates how rapidly the situation could escalate further.

cards.headline: Uganda closes border with Congo as Ebola cases rise
cards.teaser: The country shut its border after seven confirmed Ebola cases appeared in its capital.
cards.body:
Uganda closed its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as the Ebola outbreak in the neighboring country intensifies. Suspected cases in the DRC have surpassed 900, with 119 suspected deaths reported. The World Health Organization has classified the outbreak as posing a "very high" risk to the country, though it assessed the risk of global spread as low.

Uganda has confirmed seven cases of Ebola in Kampala, the capital. Officials say the country has robust disease surveillance systems in place to monitor and respond to the outbreak. Other neighboring countries have implemented border measures similar to those used during the COVID-19 pandemic to limit the virus's spread.

cards.headline: Paper mill explosion in Longview could be Washington state's deadliest modern industrial disaster
cards.teaser: A tank rupture at a Nippon paper mill has resulted in multiple deaths, with the governor calling it potentially the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington history.
cards.body:
A tank rupture at Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co in Longview, Washington has resulted in multiple deaths and missing persons. As of Wednesday afternoon, one person had died after being hospitalized, with nine others missing and presumed dead. Nine additional people were injured in the Tuesday morning incident.

Washington's governor described the disaster as potentially the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern state history. The tank held chemicals used in paper manufacturing. Authorities have transitioned from rescue to recovery operations.

cards.headline: Court orders customs chief to appear on $166 billion tariff refund compliance
cards.body:
A federal court ordered the customs chief to appear at a hearing to address compliance with refunding tariffs, signaling heightened concern about the Trump administration's efforts to repay $166 billion owed from tariffs ruled illegal.

The order represents an unusual judicial intervention requiring a senior government official to personally explain the status of refund efforts. The demand for direct testimony suggests the court views current compliance efforts as insufficient or inadequate.

The $166 billion in question stems from tariffs previously determined to have been imposed illegally. The government now faces a legal obligation to return these funds to importers and businesses who paid them.

Courts typically do not summon high-ranking officials to compliance hearings unless standard reporting mechanisms have failed or raised serious doubts. The move indicates judicial skepticism about whether the administration is meeting its repayment obligations under the law.

The hearing will require the customs chief to provide detailed information about how much has been refunded, to whom, and what timeline remains for completing the payments. Officials will need to explain any delays or obstacles preventing full compliance with the refund order.

The tariffs in question were collected over an extended period before courts ruled them unlawful. Refunding such a large sum involves identifying eligible recipients, calculating individual refund amounts, and processing payments through customs systems designed primarily for collections rather than disbursements.

Businesses that paid the tariffs have been waiting for refunds since the judicial ruling. Some companies may have included the tariff costs in their pricing to consumers, while others absorbed the expenses, affecting their bottom lines during the period when the tariffs were in effect.

The court's decision to compel testimony rather than accept written reports alone underscores the seriousness with which it views potential non-compliance. Personal appearances allow judges to question officials directly and assess credibility in real time.

The outcome of the hearing could determine whether additional enforcement measures become necessary to ensure full repayment of the illegally collected funds.

cards.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after making $1.2 million on Polymarket
cards.body:
A Google engineer has been charged with insider trading after allegedly making $1.2 million through bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. According to the criminal complaint, the engineer risked over $2.7 million on wagers related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign.

The charges suggest the engineer used non-public information about Google's internal operations to place profitable bets on outcomes tied to the company's annual search trends report. The Year in Search campaign is Google's widely publicized roundup of top search queries and trending topics from the previous year.

Polymarket allows users to bet real money on the outcomes of future events, from political elections to corporate announcements. The platform has grown in popularity as a venue for speculation on tech industry developments and company performance.

Insider trading occurs when someone trades securities or makes financial bets using material information not available to the public. Federal securities laws prohibit corporate employees from profiting off confidential company information, and violations can result in both criminal charges and civil penalties.

The complaint indicates the engineer placed multiple high-stakes wagers totaling more than $2.7 million in exposure on markets connected to Google's search data release. The bets reportedly netted $1.2 million in profits, suggesting the engineer had advance knowledge of information that would move the markets once publicly released.

Google has not publicly commented on the charges or whether the engineer remains employed at the company. The case adds to growing scrutiny of prediction markets and their potential vulnerability to exploitation by insiders with access to material non-public information.

Federal prosecutors have increasingly focused on insider trading cases involving technology company employees and contractors. The charges against the Google engineer highlight the legal risks facing employees who attempt to profit from confidential workplace information through emerging financial platforms and betting markets.

cards.headline: Packers running back Josh Jacobs released from jail, no charges filed
cards.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was released from jail after being arrested on suspicion of domestic violence. District attorneys have not filed formal charges and continue investigating the case.

Jacobs was arrested and faced potential charges including felony strangulation along with four other domestic violence related allegations. The Packers released a statement acknowledging the arrest but did not comment further on his status with the team.

Jacobs signed with Green Bay as a free agent before the current season after spending his first four years with the Las Vegas Raiders. He rushed for over 1,500 yards in his final season with the Raiders and earned Pro Bowl recognition.

The investigation remains active as prosecutors review evidence and determine whether to pursue criminal charges. Law enforcement officials have not disclosed details about the alleged incident that led to the arrest.

The NFL has not announced any disciplinary action against Jacobs. The league typically waits for the legal process to conclude before determining whether players face suspension under its personal conduct policy.

Jacobs has not made any public statements since his release from custody. The Packers have not indicated whether he will participate in upcoming team activities while the investigation continues.

Domestic violence cases in professional sports often result in league imposed penalties even when criminal charges are not filed. The NFL can act independently based on its own investigation and standards for player conduct.

The timing creates uncertainty for the Packers as they prepare for the upcoming season. Jacobs was expected to play a central role in the team's offense after his acquisition in free agency.

cards.headline: DOJ opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: The Justice Department has launched a criminal probe into whether Carroll committed perjury during a deposition.
cards.body:
Original Card (Unchanged)

The Department of Justice has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to multiple reports. CNN first reported the development Wednesday night.

The DOJ probe focuses on whether Carroll committed perjury while speaking at a deposition as part of her two civil cases against Trump. Carroll previously won two civil verdicts against the president in cases related to her sexual assault allegations and subsequent defamation claims.

---

Note: I'm returning the original card unchanged because the source material confirms the same core facts already present in your original text. The sources add minor detail (Carroll's age, the 2022 timing of the deposition, her statement about not accepting outside financial support) but don't materially alter the story's substance or require a rewrite.

cards.headline: Europe experiences record-breaking spring heat wave
cards.teaser: An exceptionally early heat wave has shattered temperature records across Western Europe and caused deaths.
cards.body:
Western Europe is gripped by an exceptionally early heat wave shattering temperature records. London has experienced temperatures reaching 95 degrees over consecutive days, while Spain and France have also broken records. The extreme conditions have resulted in deaths across affected regions and prompted government warnings.

A buckled jet stream is responsible for the record temperatures sweeping Europe. Experts attribute the unpredictable and extreme weather patterns to broader climate trends, noting that such events are becoming increasingly frequent. Officials in five European capitals are actively addressing the sustained high temperatures and implementing measures to help residents cope with the dangerous heat.

cards.headline: Ken Paxton wins Texas Senate primary, cementing Trump influence over Republican Party
cards.teaser: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton defeated incumbent Senator John Cornyn in a Republican primary runoff, underscoring Trump's continued grip on the GOP.
cards.body:
Ken Paxton defeated Senator John Cornyn in the Texas Republican Senate primary runoff, demonstrating President Trump's continued sway over party primary voters. The contentious race exposed divisions within Republican ranks, with some party operatives concerned about fundraising challenges heading into the general election.

Republicans have begun reconciling after the bruising primary battle. Democrats are now evaluating their prospects against Paxton in Texas, a state that has consistently voted Republican in recent elections.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over firefighting foam contamination
cards.teaser: The Australian government filed a lawsuit against 3M seeking $2 billion in damages over contamination from firefighting foam containing forever chemicals.
cards.body:
Australia has sued 3M for $2 billion over PFAS contamination at 28 defense bases across the country. The government is seeking to recover costs related to firefighting foam that contained the persistent chemicals.

PFAS, known as "forever chemicals," do not break down naturally in the environment. The foam was used at multiple Australian defense facilities over many years, leaving contamination at the sites.

cards.headline: Google employee charged with insider trading after making $1.2 million on bets
cards.teaser: A longtime Google information security engineer was charged with using internal company data to make $1.2 million through betting on Polymarket.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York charged Google information security engineer Michele Spagnuolo with insider trading after he allegedly used confidential company data to place profitable bets on Polymarket. Spagnuolo made approximately $1.2 million from trades related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign, wagering over $2.7 million total on the prediction market platform.

Prosecutors allege that Spagnuolo accessed Google's confidential information and used his knowledge of search trends to inform his betting decisions before the public knew the outcomes. The case marks an application of insider trading laws to cryptocurrency-based prediction markets.

cards.headline: Snowflake commits $6 billion to Amazon cloud in agentic computing expansion
cards.teaser: Snowflake agreed to spend $6 billion on Amazon Web Services as part of an expanded partnership focused on enterprise agentic AI adoption.
cards.body:
Snowflake has signed a five-year deal with Amazon Web Services to purchase $6 billion in cloud computing capacity for AI chips. The agreement expands the existing partnership between the data cloud company and AWS.

The announcement drove Snowflake's stock up 36 percent, alongside stronger-than-expected earnings results powered by AI demand. The expanded collaboration aims to support enterprise agentic AI applications that can operate autonomously on behalf of users.

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla's bid to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: A California court denied Tesla's attempt to throw out a racial discrimination lawsuit brought by the state's civil rights agency, setting the stage for a trial in July.
cards.body:
Tesla has lost its legal effort to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit filed by California's civil rights agency. The court ruling keeps the case on track and allows it to proceed to trial, which is anticipated to begin in July.

The California Civil Rights Department, which brought the lawsuit, welcomed the court's decision as a significant victory. The agency has been pursuing claims of workplace discrimination at Tesla facilities in the state. Tesla had sought to have the case dismissed before trial, but the court rejected those arguments and ruled the claims should be heard.

cards.headline: New York and New Jersey subpoena FIFA over World Cup ticket prices
cards.teaser: Attorneys general from New York and New Jersey have issued subpoenas to FIFA as part of an investigation into ticket pricing for the 2026 World Cup.
cards.body:
The attorneys general of New York and New Jersey have launched a joint investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup. The probe, announced by New York Attorney General Letitia James and New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport, centers on matches scheduled at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

The investigation focuses on complaints from fans who claim they were misled about seat locations and pricing. Officials are examining FIFA's public messaging around tickets, which they say has contributed to the inflated prices seen throughout the tournament. The subpoena seeks information on FIFA's ticketing practices related to these World Cup matches.

cards.headline: Senators Cruz and Cantwell propose bipartisan bill to reform college sports
cards.teaser: Republican Ted Cruz and Democrat Maria Cantwell introduced legislation that would impose salary caps and transfer limits on college athletics programs.
cards.body:
Republican Senator Ted Cruz and Democratic Senator Maria Cantwell unveiled bipartisan legislation called the Protect College Sports bill aimed at overhauling college athletics. The proposal includes measures to establish salary caps for athletes and restrict transfer eligibility.

The bill also targets coaching changes, specifically addressing situations like Lane Kiffin's recent move to LSU. Southeastern Conference leaders have reportedly begun discussing contingency plans in response to the proposed reforms. The legislation represents an attempt to address ongoing turmoil in college sports following recent changes to compensation and transfer rules.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she thought husband was having a stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
The former first lady told CBS News that she was frightened by Joe Biden's performance during his 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. In an interview set to air Sunday, Jill Biden said she had never seen her husband perform that way before or since, describing herself as "frightened" as she watched his faltering performance.

She said she thought Joe Biden might have suffered a stroke during the televised debate. The debate took place during the 2024 presidential campaign when Biden was seeking reelection. Trump ultimately won that election and is currently serving as president.

cards.headline: Iran restores internet access after 88-day shutdown
cards.teaser: The Iranian government is allowing people to reconnect with the world after a near-total internet blackout.
cards.body:
Iran has begun restoring internet connectivity to its population following an 88-day near-total shutdown that blocked access to news, television, and chat services. The government lifted restrictions that had cut off most Iranians from global communications during the war with the United States.

Access remains limited, with not all residents able to connect. Iranians who have regained connectivity are uncertain how long the government will allow the access to continue. The shutdown had prevented the population from receiving uncensored information during the three-month conflict.

cards.headline: Lebanese expect prolonged war despite US-Iran negotiations
cards.teaser: Clashes between Israel and Hezbollah are intensifying in southern Lebanon as residents doubt diplomatic efforts will bring peace.
cards.body:
People in Lebanon are skeptical that US-Iran peace negotiations will end the fighting in their country. As the three-month war continues, clashes between Israel and Hezbollah have intensified in southern Lebanon, with few residents believing diplomatic efforts will bring relief.

The pessimism reflects the reality on the ground: even if the US and Iran reach a deal, the conflict between Israeli forces and Hezbollah shows no signs of stopping. Lebanese residents expect the violence in their region to persist regardless of broader ceasefire negotiations.

cards.headline: Justice Department charges Google employee over Polymarket insider trading
cards.teaser: A Google staffer faces criminal charges for allegedly using insider information to net $1.2 million in profits on the prediction market platform Polymarket.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice has filed criminal charges against a Google engineer accused of using insider information to trade on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. The engineer wagered over $2.7 million on bets related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign and made approximately $1.2 million in profits.

This marks the second known federal criminal case involving alleged insider trading on a prediction market platform. The charges indicate that federal prosecutors are applying insider trading laws to these emerging financial platforms with the same rigor used for traditional securities markets.

cards.headline: Trump administration in talks to fund US drone manufacturers
cards.teaser: The Trump administration entered discussions to provide funding to American drone companies as part of efforts to support domestic manufacturing.
cards.body:
The Trump administration opened talks with US drone manufacturers about potential government funding. The discussions focus on supporting domestic production capabilities in the unmanned aerial vehicle sector.

The initiative represents a push to strengthen American drone manufacturing amid competition from foreign producers.

cards.headline: Ferrari electric vehicle launch meets criticism from investors and analysts
cards.teaser: Ferrari's first electric car faced backlash including memes, analyst skepticism, and a stock selloff following its debut.
cards.body:
Ferrari's new Luce electric vehicle has faced significant backlash following its unveiling. The model sparked negative reactions on social media, with memes mocking the car's design. Analysts raised concerns about its market viability, and investors responded by selling Ferrari stock.

The criticism reflects broader anxieties about the automaker's direction. A former Ferrari chairman cautioned that the electric model could damage the company's legendary status. The negative reception has been particularly pronounced in Italy, where Ferrari holds deep cultural importance as a national icon.

cards.headline: Rivian to deliver first R2 SUVs on June 9
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker set a delivery date for its new R2 SUV, which CEO RJ Scaringe called perhaps the most important product the company has launched.
cards.body:
Rivian has set June 9 as the date for first customer deliveries of its R2 SUV. CEO RJ Scaringe has called the vehicle "maybe the most important thing we've launched to date."

The R2 marks a significant milestone for the electric vehicle maker as it works to expand its product lineup and reach new customers.

cards.headline: Dodgers place Kiké Hernández back on injured list with oblique tear
cards.teaser: The Los Angeles Dodgers returned infielder Enrique Hernández to the injured list after he suffered a significant oblique tear just two games into his comeback.
cards.body:
Kiké Hernández returned to the Dodgers injured list with a left oblique strain after playing only two games following his previous absence. Medical evaluation revealed a significant tear that will sideline the veteran infielder.

The Dodgers recalled a player from Triple-A to fill Hernández's roster spot. Hernández had recently made what was described as an emotional return to the lineup and contributed to a victory over the Colorado Rockies before the injury recurrence forced him back out of action.

cards.headline: Crystal Palace wins European trophy without midfielder Adam Wharton
cards.teaser: Adam Wharton excelled as Crystal Palace captured a Conference League title, but the midfielder will not play for England at the World Cup.
cards.body:
Crystal Palace won the Conference League final, with Jean-Philippe Mateta scoring the decisive goal against Rayo Vallecano. The victory marks manager Oliver Glasner's final match in charge and caps a remarkable 12 months that has seen him win three trophies: the FA Cup, Community Shield, and Conference League.

The triumph provides some redemption after Palace were denied a place in this season's Europa League due to breaches of UEFA's multi-club ownership rules, despite winning last year's FA Cup. Glasner celebrated the win with a full-length slide on the pitch, while thousands of supporters back at Selhurst Park invaded the pitch as they watched on a big screen.

cards.headline: Spielberg Says Hollywood Should Never Use AI for Creative Decisions
cards.body:
Director Steven Spielberg spoke against using artificial intelligence in creative filmmaking during a recent appearance on Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson's IMO podcast. Spielberg said he thinks AI can help solve medical issues, but opposes its use in the creative process.

"Where I don't love AI is where" it takes over creative decisions in Hollywood, Spielberg said. He drew a clear line on the technology's role in the industry, stating that AI should never serve as the final word on anything creative.

The comments come as the film industry debates AI's expanding role in production. Studios have explored using AI for visual effects, script analysis, and other production tasks. Spielberg's position represents a cautious approach from one of Hollywood's most influential directors.

Spielberg has directed films including Jaws, E.T., Schindler's List, and Saving Private Ryan over a career spanning five decades. His stance on AI adds weight to ongoing conversations about technology's limits in artistic fields.

The director did not specify which particular AI applications in filmmaking concerned him most. He also did not address whether AI tools could assist in technical aspects of production separate from creative choices.

Other filmmakers and industry figures have expressed mixed views on AI in recent years. Some see potential for efficiency gains, while others worry about job displacement and artistic integrity. Spielberg's comments align with those raising concerns about preserving human creativity in the filmmaking process.

The podcast appearance covered other topics beyond artificial intelligence. Spielberg discussed his career and experiences in the entertainment industry with hosts Obama and Robinson.

cards.headline: US military strikes Iranian drone site as negotiations continue
cards.body:
The US military struck an Iranian ground control station and shot down four Iranian one-way attack drones in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, a senior US official said. US Central Command said its forces intercepted the drones that posed a threat to commercial shipping in the area.

The strike targeted a ground control station in Bandar Abbas, a port city on Iran's southern coast, that was preparing to launch a fifth drone, according to a US official speaking on condition of anonymity. The official said the US military attacked the Iranian drone-launching unit on the ground after shooting down the initial four drones.

This marks the second military clash between US and Iranian forces in 48 hours. The skirmish occurred as the US and Iran are negotiating a deal to end the ongoing war between the two nations.

President Donald Trump addressed the situation during a Cabinet meeting, his remarks differing from statements he made over the weekend suggesting an agreement to end the war with Iran was close. Trump held to what were described as maximum demands on Iran during the meeting.

The incident in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil shipments, targeted a commercial vessel. US forces intervened to eliminate the threat posed by the Iranian drones to shipping traffic in the strategic passage.

The timing of the military action complicates ongoing diplomatic efforts. The US and Iran have been engaged in talks aimed at resolving the conflict, but Wednesday's exchange of fire underscores the fragility of the negotiation process.

US Central Command confirmed its forces conducted the operation in response to the immediate threat. The command said the action was taken to protect commercial shipping and maintain freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-fifth of global oil consumption passes.

cards.headline: Former judges ask court to probe Trump IRS settlement
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former federal judges wants a court to reopen Trump's lawsuit against the IRS over a $1.776 billion settlement fund.
cards.body:
A bipartisan group of former federal judges filed a request on Wednesday to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. They argue the administration bypassed proper judicial oversight by negotiating a settlement rather than allowing the court to resolve the case.

The settlement established a $1.776 billion fund intended to compensate those who claim government wrongdoing. The former judges contend this arrangement circumvented necessary court supervision of the dispute between Trump and the IRS.

cards.headline: Appeals court allows pro-Palestinian activist to remain free pending Supreme Court appeal
cards.teaser: A federal appeals panel ruled that Mahmoud Khalil can stay out of custody while he petitions the Supreme Court.
cards.body:
A federal appeals court panel allowed pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil to remain free on Tuesday as he pursues his case against the Trump administration at the Supreme Court. The three-judge panel included jurists appointed by Presidents Trump, George W. Bush, and Joe Biden.

Judges Stephanos Bibas, Arianna Freeman, and Thomas Hardiman issued the order keeping Khalil out of custody while he advances his Supreme Court petition.

cards.headline: Zelensky asks Trump and Congress for Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: The Ukrainian president urged US leaders to supply air defense systems to help end the conflict with Russia.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged President Trump and members of Congress on Wednesday to supply Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors. He said the systems would help end Ukraine's conflict with Russia.

Zelensky said Ukraine has succeeded in defending against drones but has not built its own capability to produce anti-missile defense systems. He made the appeal directly to US leadership for the advanced air defense technology.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures images of Mars during flyby
cards.teaser: NASA's Psyche spacecraft photographed Mars in high resolution during a flyby on its journey to study a distant asteroid.
cards.body:
A NASA spacecraft snapped detailed images of Mars during a flyby while traveling toward its ultimate destination in the asteroid belt. The Psyche mission, which is headed to study a metal-rich asteroid, passed close enough to Mars to capture high-resolution photographs of the planet's surface.

The flyby provided unique views of Mars, including images of the planet's south polar region. The Psyche spacecraft used the encounter as an opportunity to test its imaging systems and gather scientific data while en route to its primary target, a distant asteroid that scientists believe may be the exposed core of an early planet.

cards.headline: Lamar Jackson says Ravens coaching change brings fresh perspective
cards.teaser: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson described the team's coaching transition as feeling like a breath of fresh air during organized team activities.
cards.body:
Lamar Jackson spoke positively about the Ravens coaching changes, saying new coordinator Declan Doyle is making his job easier. The quarterback expressed enthusiasm about the fresh approach to the offense.

Jackson declined to discuss his contract negotiations but said his commitment to Baltimore has not wavered. He indicated he wants to move past conversations about fully guaranteed contracts and focus on the upcoming season under the new coaching staff.

cards.headline: ABC News and National Geographic Lead News Emmy Winners
cards.teaser: ABC News won eight awards at the 47th annual News Emmys, with National Geographic taking seven prizes.
cards.body:
ABC News topped the 47th annual News Emmy Awards with eight wins overall. The network's World News Tonight with David Muir claimed the outstanding live news program award for the second year running.

National Geographic followed with seven News Emmys, bolstered by recognition for Trafficked with Mariana van Zeller. Both networks are owned by Disney.

cards.headline: Student Winner Criticizes CBS News in Emmy Acceptance Speech
cards.teaser: A high school senior accepting a journalism scholarship named after Mike Wallace criticized CBS News during the News Emmy Awards ceremony.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior at District of Columbia International School in Washington, criticized CBS News while accepting the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy Awards. He said the recent direction of the outlet stains the legacy of Mike Wallace.

Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the scholarship, which is named after the longtime CBS journalist. Campos addressed the crowd during his acceptance speech.

cards.headline: Horror Film Obsession Sees Rare Box Office Increase in Second Weekend
cards.teaser: The A24 horror film Obsession increased its box office earnings in its second weekend of release.
cards.body:
Obsession posted a second-weekend box office increase, an uncommon occurrence in theatrical releases. The film has become a breakout summer hit at theaters.

The performance marked the first time a film has achieved this pattern since Sound of Freedom. Obsession is distributed by A24.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans endorse Paxton after primary win over Cornyn
cards.teaser: Senate leadership is working to unify the party behind Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following his costly primary victory.
cards.body:
Senate Republican leaders are working to mend relationships with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and signal support from major donors as they seek to maintain their majority. Senate Majority Leader John Thune spoke with Paxton by phone on Wednesday before endorsing him on a radio show.

The effort follows a $130 million Senate primary in which Paxton defeated Senator John Cornyn. Republican leaders want to move past the contentious primary battle and focus on the general election against the Democratic nominee.

cards.headline: Analysis of thousands of Trump social media posts reveals patterns
cards.teaser: BBC Verify examined thousands of President Trump's social media posts to identify trends and patterns in his online communication.
cards.body:
The BBC's Ros Atkins and the BBC Verify team analysed thousands of President Trump's social media posts to identify patterns in his communication style and focus areas. The examination reviewed his prolific output across social platforms.

The systematic review of Trump's digital communications was presented as part of the BBC's coverage of American politics and the Trump administration's communication strategies.

cards.headline: Donkey Kong 64 coming to Nintendo Switch Online next week
cards.teaser: Nintendo will add the N64 game Donkey Kong 64 to its Switch Online subscription service next week.
cards.body:
Nintendo announced that Donkey Kong 64 will join the Nintendo Switch Online library of N64 games next week. The 1999 platform adventure game will become available to subscribers of the service's expansion tier, which provides access to classic games from older Nintendo consoles.

Donkey Kong 64 was originally released for the Nintendo 64 and featured the barrel-throwing ape in a three-dimensional collect-a-thon adventure. The addition expands Nintendo Switch Online's growing catalog of retro titles available for streaming on the current-generation console.

cards.headline: Morris Day Denies Performing at Freedom 250 Concert After Backlash
cards.teaser: Singer Morris Day said he will not perform at a National Mall concert despite being listed in the announced lineup.
cards.body:
Morris Day has denied reports that he and the Time will perform at the Freedom 250 concert scheduled for June 27 on the National Mall in Washington. The organizers had announced him as a headliner for the event, which is part of a 16-day patriotic celebration marking the country's 250th anniversary.

Day's denial came after backlash from fans who criticized his involvement. Other performers announced for the Freedom 250 lineup include Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice.

cards.headline: Kanye Label Executive Sues to Identify Anonymous Figure Behind Websites
cards.teaser: Larry Jackson filed a lawsuit seeking to unmask an anonymous person he says created defamatory websites targeting him.
cards.body:
Larry Jackson, a label executive associated with Kanye West, filed a lawsuit seeking to unmask an anonymous person operating websites against him. Jackson claims the individual is conducting what he describes as "reputational warfare" designed to damage his reputation.

The legal action asks a judge to help identify the mystery figure behind the sites. Jackson characterizes the activity as an attempt to destroy him through the online campaign.

hero.headline: US conducts second round of strikes on Iran in three days
hero.body:
The United States carried out fresh military strikes against Iranian targets in southern Iran on Wednesday, representing the second offensive operation within three days as a ceasefire between the two nations remains fragile and peace negotiations continue.

According to US officials, the strikes were executed as a defensive measure in response to Iranian military activity. The attacks targeted four one-way attack drones and a drone ground-control station operated by Iranian forces at military sites in the region.

These operations risk destabilizing the currently tenuous ceasefire that has been holding between the two countries. Diplomatic efforts to resolve the three-month conflict remain ongoing, though military escalation threatens to undermine the negotiation process.

The strikes triggered immediate market reactions, with oil prices climbing sharply as investors grew concerned about potential disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most critical trade corridors for energy transport. Approximately 20 percent of global crude oil passes through this narrow waterway, making any threat to its security a significant economic concern.

When asked about the strikes, President Trump stated he faces no political pressure to reach an agreement with Iran ahead of midterm elections. He indicated a willingness to outlast Iranian negotiators in talks and suggested electoral considerations would not shape his approach to the conflict.

The three-month war has already caused substantial damage to regional infrastructure. Recent Iranian drone strikes hit Kuwait's oil sector, causing severe damage to petrochemical plants and other facilities. Similar attacks have struck targets in the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain. These incidents have contributed to what analysts describe as the largest disruption to oil supplies in history, with Brent crude prices rising significantly from earlier in the year.

The conflict has also had spillover effects in neighboring countries. In Lebanon, clashes between Israel and Hezbollah have intensified in the southern regions, leaving residents skeptical that US-Iran negotiations will ease violence affecting their territory.

Meanwhile, Iran has begun restoring internet access to its population following an 88-day near-total shutdown. The government has allowed some users to reconnect to services previously blocked, though access remains limited and uncertain. Many Iranians question how long the restored connectivity will persist.

The Pentagon characterized Wednesday's strikes as defensive responses to immediate threats from Iranian drone operations. Military officials have not announced plans for additional military action at this time, though the volatile situation demonstrates how rapidly the situation could escalate further.

cards.headline: Uganda closes border with Congo as Ebola cases rise
cards.teaser: The country shut its border after seven confirmed Ebola cases appeared in its capital.
cards.body:
Uganda closed its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as the Ebola outbreak in the neighboring country intensifies. Suspected cases in the DRC have surpassed 900, with 119 suspected deaths reported. The World Health Organization has classified the outbreak as posing a "very high" risk to the country, though it assessed the risk of global spread as low.

Uganda has confirmed seven cases of Ebola in Kampala, the capital. Officials say the country has robust disease surveillance systems in place to monitor and respond to the outbreak. Other neighboring countries have implemented border measures similar to those used during the COVID-19 pandemic to limit the virus's spread.

cards.headline: Europe experiences record-breaking spring heat wave
cards.teaser: An exceptionally early heat wave has shattered temperature records across Western Europe and caused deaths.
cards.body:
Western Europe is gripped by an exceptionally early heat wave shattering temperature records. London has experienced temperatures reaching 95 degrees over consecutive days, while Spain and France have also broken records. The extreme conditions have resulted in deaths across affected regions and prompted government warnings.

A buckled jet stream is responsible for the record temperatures sweeping Europe. Experts attribute the unpredictable and extreme weather patterns to broader climate trends, noting that such events are becoming increasingly frequent. Officials in five European capitals are actively addressing the sustained high temperatures and implementing measures to help residents cope with the dangerous heat.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she thought husband was having a stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
The former first lady told CBS News that she was frightened by Joe Biden's performance during his 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. In an interview set to air Sunday, Jill Biden said she had never seen her husband perform that way before or since, describing herself as "frightened" as she watched his faltering performance.

She said she thought Joe Biden might have suffered a stroke during the televised debate. The debate took place during the 2024 presidential campaign when Biden was seeking reelection. Trump ultimately won that election and is currently serving as president.

cards.headline: Iran restores internet access after 88-day shutdown
cards.teaser: The Iranian government is allowing people to reconnect with the world after a near-total internet blackout.
cards.body:
Iran has begun restoring internet connectivity to its population following an 88-day near-total shutdown that blocked access to news, television, and chat services. The government lifted restrictions that had cut off most Iranians from global communications during the war with the United States.

Access remains limited, with not all residents able to connect. Iranians who have regained connectivity are uncertain how long the government will allow the access to continue. The shutdown had prevented the population from receiving uncensored information during the three-month conflict.

cards.headline: Lebanese expect prolonged war despite US-Iran negotiations
cards.teaser: Clashes between Israel and Hezbollah are intensifying in southern Lebanon as residents doubt diplomatic efforts will bring peace.
cards.body:
People in Lebanon are skeptical that US-Iran peace negotiations will end the fighting in their country. As the three-month war continues, clashes between Israel and Hezbollah have intensified in southern Lebanon, with few residents believing diplomatic efforts will bring relief.

The pessimism reflects the reality on the ground: even if the US and Iran reach a deal, the conflict between Israeli forces and Hezbollah shows no signs of stopping. Lebanese residents expect the violence in their region to persist regardless of broader ceasefire negotiations.

hero.headline: US strikes Iran for second time in three days during fragile ceasefire
hero.body:
The United States conducted military strikes against targets in Iran for the second time in three days, according to reports. The attacks targeted a drone launch site as hostilities continued during what has been described as a fragile ceasefire between the two nations.

The strikes come as the US and Iran remain engaged in negotiations aimed at ending a three-month war. President Trump has maintained what sources describe as maximum demands on Iran during the talks. The conflict has raised concerns about disruption to shipping in the strategically important Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil transit.

Oil markets responded to the renewed strikes, with prices jumping on fears that disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz could affect global supply. The waterway handles a significant portion of the world's petroleum shipments, making any military action in the region a concern for energy markets.

The strikes occurred despite ongoing diplomatic efforts to reach an accord between Washington and Tehran. According to multiple reports, no agreement appears imminent as Trump continues to hold firm on his negotiating position. The president has reportedly expressed indifference to political pressure related to the midterm elections as the military actions continue.

The three-month conflict represents one of the most significant direct military confrontations between the United States and Iran. Previous tensions between the nations had typically involved proxy forces or more limited engagements, making the current sustained hostilities notable in the history of US-Iran relations.

The timing of the strikes, occurring during ceasefire negotiations, highlights the precarious nature of the current diplomatic process. Military officials have not provided detailed information about the specific targets hit or the extent of damage caused by the latest round of strikes.

The situation remains fluid as both military operations and diplomatic talks continue simultaneously. The international community has expressed concern about the potential for the conflict to escalate further or to disrupt vital shipping lanes that serve as arteries for global commerce.

cards.headline: Paper mill explosion in Longview could be Washington state's deadliest modern industrial disaster
cards.teaser: A tank rupture at a Nippon paper mill has resulted in multiple deaths, with the governor calling it potentially the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington history.
cards.body:
A tank rupture at Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co in Longview, Washington has resulted in multiple deaths and missing persons. As of Wednesday afternoon, one person had died after being hospitalized, with nine others missing and presumed dead. Nine additional people were injured in the Tuesday morning incident.

Washington's governor described the disaster as potentially the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern state history. The tank held chemicals used in paper manufacturing. Authorities have transitioned from rescue to recovery operations.

cards.headline: Ken Paxton wins Texas Senate primary, cementing Trump influence over Republican Party
cards.teaser: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton defeated incumbent Senator John Cornyn in a Republican primary runoff, underscoring Trump's continued grip on the GOP.
cards.body:
Ken Paxton defeated Senator John Cornyn in the Texas Republican Senate primary runoff, demonstrating President Trump's continued sway over party primary voters. The contentious race exposed divisions within Republican ranks, with some party operatives concerned about fundraising challenges heading into the general election.

Republicans have begun reconciling after the bruising primary battle. Democrats are now evaluating their prospects against Paxton in Texas, a state that has consistently voted Republican in recent elections.

cards.headline: Justice Department charges Google employee over Polymarket insider trading
cards.teaser: A Google staffer faces criminal charges for allegedly using insider information to net $1.2 million in profits on the prediction market platform Polymarket.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice has filed criminal charges against a Google engineer accused of using insider information to trade on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. The engineer wagered over $2.7 million on bets related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign and made approximately $1.2 million in profits.

This marks the second known federal criminal case involving alleged insider trading on a prediction market platform. The charges indicate that federal prosecutors are applying insider trading laws to these emerging financial platforms with the same rigor used for traditional securities markets.

cards.headline: Analysis of thousands of Trump social media posts reveals patterns
cards.teaser: BBC Verify examined thousands of President Trump's social media posts to identify trends and patterns in his online communication.
cards.body:
The BBC's Ros Atkins and the BBC Verify team analysed thousands of President Trump's social media posts to identify patterns in his communication style and focus areas. The examination reviewed his prolific output across social platforms.

The systematic review of Trump's digital communications was presented as part of the BBC's coverage of American politics and the Trump administration's communication strategies.

hero.headline: Court orders customs chief to appear on $166 billion tariff refund compliance
hero.body:
A federal court ordered the customs chief to appear at a hearing to address compliance with refunding tariffs, signaling heightened concern about the Trump administration's efforts to repay $166 billion owed from tariffs ruled illegal.

The order represents an unusual judicial intervention requiring a senior government official to personally explain the status of refund efforts. The demand for direct testimony suggests the court views current compliance efforts as insufficient or inadequate.

The $166 billion in question stems from tariffs previously determined to have been imposed illegally. The government now faces a legal obligation to return these funds to importers and businesses who paid them.

Courts typically do not summon high-ranking officials to compliance hearings unless standard reporting mechanisms have failed or raised serious doubts. The move indicates judicial skepticism about whether the administration is meeting its repayment obligations under the law.

The hearing will require the customs chief to provide detailed information about how much has been refunded, to whom, and what timeline remains for completing the payments. Officials will need to explain any delays or obstacles preventing full compliance with the refund order.

The tariffs in question were collected over an extended period before courts ruled them unlawful. Refunding such a large sum involves identifying eligible recipients, calculating individual refund amounts, and processing payments through customs systems designed primarily for collections rather than disbursements.

Businesses that paid the tariffs have been waiting for refunds since the judicial ruling. Some companies may have included the tariff costs in their pricing to consumers, while others absorbed the expenses, affecting their bottom lines during the period when the tariffs were in effect.

The court's decision to compel testimony rather than accept written reports alone underscores the seriousness with which it views potential non-compliance. Personal appearances allow judges to question officials directly and assess credibility in real time.

The outcome of the hearing could determine whether additional enforcement measures become necessary to ensure full repayment of the illegally collected funds.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over firefighting foam contamination
cards.teaser: The Australian government filed a lawsuit against 3M seeking $2 billion in damages over contamination from firefighting foam containing forever chemicals.
cards.body:
Australia has sued 3M for $2 billion over PFAS contamination at 28 defense bases across the country. The government is seeking to recover costs related to firefighting foam that contained the persistent chemicals.

PFAS, known as "forever chemicals," do not break down naturally in the environment. The foam was used at multiple Australian defense facilities over many years, leaving contamination at the sites.

cards.headline: Google employee charged with insider trading after making $1.2 million on bets
cards.teaser: A longtime Google information security engineer was charged with using internal company data to make $1.2 million through betting on Polymarket.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York charged Google information security engineer Michele Spagnuolo with insider trading after he allegedly used confidential company data to place profitable bets on Polymarket. Spagnuolo made approximately $1.2 million from trades related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign, wagering over $2.7 million total on the prediction market platform.

Prosecutors allege that Spagnuolo accessed Google's confidential information and used his knowledge of search trends to inform his betting decisions before the public knew the outcomes. The case marks an application of insider trading laws to cryptocurrency-based prediction markets.

cards.headline: Snowflake commits $6 billion to Amazon cloud in agentic computing expansion
cards.teaser: Snowflake agreed to spend $6 billion on Amazon Web Services as part of an expanded partnership focused on enterprise agentic AI adoption.
cards.body:
Snowflake has signed a five-year deal with Amazon Web Services to purchase $6 billion in cloud computing capacity for AI chips. The agreement expands the existing partnership between the data cloud company and AWS.

The announcement drove Snowflake's stock up 36 percent, alongside stronger-than-expected earnings results powered by AI demand. The expanded collaboration aims to support enterprise agentic AI applications that can operate autonomously on behalf of users.

cards.headline: Trump administration in talks to fund US drone manufacturers
cards.teaser: The Trump administration entered discussions to provide funding to American drone companies as part of efforts to support domestic manufacturing.
cards.body:
The Trump administration opened talks with US drone manufacturers about potential government funding. The discussions focus on supporting domestic production capabilities in the unmanned aerial vehicle sector.

The initiative represents a push to strengthen American drone manufacturing amid competition from foreign producers.

cards.headline: Ferrari electric vehicle launch meets criticism from investors and analysts
cards.teaser: Ferrari's first electric car faced backlash including memes, analyst skepticism, and a stock selloff following its debut.
cards.body:
Ferrari's new Luce electric vehicle has faced significant backlash following its unveiling. The model sparked negative reactions on social media, with memes mocking the car's design. Analysts raised concerns about its market viability, and investors responded by selling Ferrari stock.

The criticism reflects broader anxieties about the automaker's direction. A former Ferrari chairman cautioned that the electric model could damage the company's legendary status. The negative reception has been particularly pronounced in Italy, where Ferrari holds deep cultural importance as a national icon.

hero.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after making $1.2 million on Polymarket
hero.body:
A Google engineer has been charged with insider trading after allegedly making $1.2 million through bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. According to the criminal complaint, the engineer risked over $2.7 million on wagers related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign.

The charges suggest the engineer used non-public information about Google's internal operations to place profitable bets on outcomes tied to the company's annual search trends report. The Year in Search campaign is Google's widely publicized roundup of top search queries and trending topics from the previous year.

Polymarket allows users to bet real money on the outcomes of future events, from political elections to corporate announcements. The platform has grown in popularity as a venue for speculation on tech industry developments and company performance.

Insider trading occurs when someone trades securities or makes financial bets using material information not available to the public. Federal securities laws prohibit corporate employees from profiting off confidential company information, and violations can result in both criminal charges and civil penalties.

The complaint indicates the engineer placed multiple high-stakes wagers totaling more than $2.7 million in exposure on markets connected to Google's search data release. The bets reportedly netted $1.2 million in profits, suggesting the engineer had advance knowledge of information that would move the markets once publicly released.

Google has not publicly commented on the charges or whether the engineer remains employed at the company. The case adds to growing scrutiny of prediction markets and their potential vulnerability to exploitation by insiders with access to material non-public information.

Federal prosecutors have increasingly focused on insider trading cases involving technology company employees and contractors. The charges against the Google engineer highlight the legal risks facing employees who attempt to profit from confidential workplace information through emerging financial platforms and betting markets.

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla's bid to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: A California court denied Tesla's attempt to throw out a racial discrimination lawsuit brought by the state's civil rights agency, setting the stage for a trial in July.
cards.body:
Tesla has lost its legal effort to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit filed by California's civil rights agency. The court ruling keeps the case on track and allows it to proceed to trial, which is anticipated to begin in July.

The California Civil Rights Department, which brought the lawsuit, welcomed the court's decision as a significant victory. The agency has been pursuing claims of workplace discrimination at Tesla facilities in the state. Tesla had sought to have the case dismissed before trial, but the court rejected those arguments and ruled the claims should be heard.

cards.headline: Rivian to deliver first R2 SUVs on June 9
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker set a delivery date for its new R2 SUV, which CEO RJ Scaringe called perhaps the most important product the company has launched.
cards.body:
Rivian has set June 9 as the date for first customer deliveries of its R2 SUV. CEO RJ Scaringe has called the vehicle "maybe the most important thing we've launched to date."

The R2 marks a significant milestone for the electric vehicle maker as it works to expand its product lineup and reach new customers.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures images of Mars during flyby
cards.teaser: NASA's Psyche spacecraft photographed Mars in high resolution during a flyby on its journey to study a distant asteroid.
cards.body:
A NASA spacecraft snapped detailed images of Mars during a flyby while traveling toward its ultimate destination in the asteroid belt. The Psyche mission, which is headed to study a metal-rich asteroid, passed close enough to Mars to capture high-resolution photographs of the planet's surface.

The flyby provided unique views of Mars, including images of the planet's south polar region. The Psyche spacecraft used the encounter as an opportunity to test its imaging systems and gather scientific data while en route to its primary target, a distant asteroid that scientists believe may be the exposed core of an early planet.

cards.headline: Donkey Kong 64 coming to Nintendo Switch Online next week
cards.teaser: Nintendo will add the N64 game Donkey Kong 64 to its Switch Online subscription service next week.
cards.body:
Nintendo announced that Donkey Kong 64 will join the Nintendo Switch Online library of N64 games next week. The 1999 platform adventure game will become available to subscribers of the service's expansion tier, which provides access to classic games from older Nintendo consoles.

Donkey Kong 64 was originally released for the Nintendo 64 and featured the barrel-throwing ape in a three-dimensional collect-a-thon adventure. The addition expands Nintendo Switch Online's growing catalog of retro titles available for streaming on the current-generation console.

hero.headline: Packers running back Josh Jacobs released from jail, no charges filed
hero.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was released from jail after being arrested on suspicion of domestic violence. District attorneys have not filed formal charges and continue investigating the case.

Jacobs was arrested and faced potential charges including felony strangulation along with four other domestic violence related allegations. The Packers released a statement acknowledging the arrest but did not comment further on his status with the team.

Jacobs signed with Green Bay as a free agent before the current season after spending his first four years with the Las Vegas Raiders. He rushed for over 1,500 yards in his final season with the Raiders and earned Pro Bowl recognition.

The investigation remains active as prosecutors review evidence and determine whether to pursue criminal charges. Law enforcement officials have not disclosed details about the alleged incident that led to the arrest.

The NFL has not announced any disciplinary action against Jacobs. The league typically waits for the legal process to conclude before determining whether players face suspension under its personal conduct policy.

Jacobs has not made any public statements since his release from custody. The Packers have not indicated whether he will participate in upcoming team activities while the investigation continues.

Domestic violence cases in professional sports often result in league imposed penalties even when criminal charges are not filed. The NFL can act independently based on its own investigation and standards for player conduct.

The timing creates uncertainty for the Packers as they prepare for the upcoming season. Jacobs was expected to play a central role in the team's offense after his acquisition in free agency.

cards.headline: New York and New Jersey subpoena FIFA over World Cup ticket prices
cards.teaser: Attorneys general from New York and New Jersey have issued subpoenas to FIFA as part of an investigation into ticket pricing for the 2026 World Cup.
cards.body:
The attorneys general of New York and New Jersey have launched a joint investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup. The probe, announced by New York Attorney General Letitia James and New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport, centers on matches scheduled at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

The investigation focuses on complaints from fans who claim they were misled about seat locations and pricing. Officials are examining FIFA's public messaging around tickets, which they say has contributed to the inflated prices seen throughout the tournament. The subpoena seeks information on FIFA's ticketing practices related to these World Cup matches.

cards.headline: Senators Cruz and Cantwell propose bipartisan bill to reform college sports
cards.teaser: Republican Ted Cruz and Democrat Maria Cantwell introduced legislation that would impose salary caps and transfer limits on college athletics programs.
cards.body:
Republican Senator Ted Cruz and Democratic Senator Maria Cantwell unveiled bipartisan legislation called the Protect College Sports bill aimed at overhauling college athletics. The proposal includes measures to establish salary caps for athletes and restrict transfer eligibility.

The bill also targets coaching changes, specifically addressing situations like Lane Kiffin's recent move to LSU. Southeastern Conference leaders have reportedly begun discussing contingency plans in response to the proposed reforms. The legislation represents an attempt to address ongoing turmoil in college sports following recent changes to compensation and transfer rules.

cards.headline: Dodgers place Kiké Hernández back on injured list with oblique tear
cards.teaser: The Los Angeles Dodgers returned infielder Enrique Hernández to the injured list after he suffered a significant oblique tear just two games into his comeback.
cards.body:
Kiké Hernández returned to the Dodgers injured list with a left oblique strain after playing only two games following his previous absence. Medical evaluation revealed a significant tear that will sideline the veteran infielder.

The Dodgers recalled a player from Triple-A to fill Hernández's roster spot. Hernández had recently made what was described as an emotional return to the lineup and contributed to a victory over the Colorado Rockies before the injury recurrence forced him back out of action.

cards.headline: Crystal Palace wins European trophy without midfielder Adam Wharton
cards.teaser: Adam Wharton excelled as Crystal Palace captured a Conference League title, but the midfielder will not play for England at the World Cup.
cards.body:
Crystal Palace won the Conference League final, with Jean-Philippe Mateta scoring the decisive goal against Rayo Vallecano. The victory marks manager Oliver Glasner's final match in charge and caps a remarkable 12 months that has seen him win three trophies: the FA Cup, Community Shield, and Conference League.

The triumph provides some redemption after Palace were denied a place in this season's Europa League due to breaches of UEFA's multi-club ownership rules, despite winning last year's FA Cup. Glasner celebrated the win with a full-length slide on the pitch, while thousands of supporters back at Selhurst Park invaded the pitch as they watched on a big screen.

cards.headline: Lamar Jackson says Ravens coaching change brings fresh perspective
cards.teaser: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson described the team's coaching transition as feeling like a breath of fresh air during organized team activities.
cards.body:
Lamar Jackson spoke positively about the Ravens coaching changes, saying new coordinator Declan Doyle is making his job easier. The quarterback expressed enthusiasm about the fresh approach to the offense.

Jackson declined to discuss his contract negotiations but said his commitment to Baltimore has not wavered. He indicated he wants to move past conversations about fully guaranteed contracts and focus on the upcoming season under the new coaching staff.

hero.headline: Spielberg Says Hollywood Should Never Use AI for Creative Decisions
hero.body:
Director Steven Spielberg spoke against using artificial intelligence in creative filmmaking during a recent appearance on Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson's IMO podcast. Spielberg said he thinks AI can help solve medical issues, but opposes its use in the creative process.

"Where I don't love AI is where" it takes over creative decisions in Hollywood, Spielberg said. He drew a clear line on the technology's role in the industry, stating that AI should never serve as the final word on anything creative.

The comments come as the film industry debates AI's expanding role in production. Studios have explored using AI for visual effects, script analysis, and other production tasks. Spielberg's position represents a cautious approach from one of Hollywood's most influential directors.

Spielberg has directed films including Jaws, E.T., Schindler's List, and Saving Private Ryan over a career spanning five decades. His stance on AI adds weight to ongoing conversations about technology's limits in artistic fields.

The director did not specify which particular AI applications in filmmaking concerned him most. He also did not address whether AI tools could assist in technical aspects of production separate from creative choices.

Other filmmakers and industry figures have expressed mixed views on AI in recent years. Some see potential for efficiency gains, while others worry about job displacement and artistic integrity. Spielberg's comments align with those raising concerns about preserving human creativity in the filmmaking process.

The podcast appearance covered other topics beyond artificial intelligence. Spielberg discussed his career and experiences in the entertainment industry with hosts Obama and Robinson.

cards.headline: ABC News and National Geographic Lead News Emmy Winners
cards.teaser: ABC News won eight awards at the 47th annual News Emmys, with National Geographic taking seven prizes.
cards.body:
ABC News topped the 47th annual News Emmy Awards with eight wins overall. The network's World News Tonight with David Muir claimed the outstanding live news program award for the second year running.

National Geographic followed with seven News Emmys, bolstered by recognition for Trafficked with Mariana van Zeller. Both networks are owned by Disney.

cards.headline: Student Winner Criticizes CBS News in Emmy Acceptance Speech
cards.teaser: A high school senior accepting a journalism scholarship named after Mike Wallace criticized CBS News during the News Emmy Awards ceremony.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior at District of Columbia International School in Washington, criticized CBS News while accepting the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy Awards. He said the recent direction of the outlet stains the legacy of Mike Wallace.

Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the scholarship, which is named after the longtime CBS journalist. Campos addressed the crowd during his acceptance speech.

cards.headline: Morris Day Denies Performing at Freedom 250 Concert After Backlash
cards.teaser: Singer Morris Day said he will not perform at a National Mall concert despite being listed in the announced lineup.
cards.body:
Morris Day has denied reports that he and the Time will perform at the Freedom 250 concert scheduled for June 27 on the National Mall in Washington. The organizers had announced him as a headliner for the event, which is part of a 16-day patriotic celebration marking the country's 250th anniversary.

Day's denial came after backlash from fans who criticized his involvement. Other performers announced for the Freedom 250 lineup include Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice.

cards.headline: Horror Film Obsession Sees Rare Box Office Increase in Second Weekend
cards.teaser: The A24 horror film Obsession increased its box office earnings in its second weekend of release.
cards.body:
Obsession posted a second-weekend box office increase, an uncommon occurrence in theatrical releases. The film has become a breakout summer hit at theaters.

The performance marked the first time a film has achieved this pattern since Sound of Freedom. Obsession is distributed by A24.

cards.headline: Kanye Label Executive Sues to Identify Anonymous Figure Behind Websites
cards.teaser: Larry Jackson filed a lawsuit seeking to unmask an anonymous person he says created defamatory websites targeting him.
cards.body:
Larry Jackson, a label executive associated with Kanye West, filed a lawsuit seeking to unmask an anonymous person operating websites against him. Jackson claims the individual is conducting what he describes as "reputational warfare" designed to damage his reputation.

The legal action asks a judge to help identify the mystery figure behind the sites. Jackson characterizes the activity as an attempt to destroy him through the online campaign.

hero.headline: US military strikes Iranian drone site as negotiations continue
hero.body:
The US military struck an Iranian ground control station and shot down four Iranian one-way attack drones in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, a senior US official said. US Central Command said its forces intercepted the drones that posed a threat to commercial shipping in the area.

The strike targeted a ground control station in Bandar Abbas, a port city on Iran's southern coast, that was preparing to launch a fifth drone, according to a US official speaking on condition of anonymity. The official said the US military attacked the Iranian drone-launching unit on the ground after shooting down the initial four drones.

This marks the second military clash between US and Iranian forces in 48 hours. The skirmish occurred as the US and Iran are negotiating a deal to end the ongoing war between the two nations.

President Donald Trump addressed the situation during a Cabinet meeting, his remarks differing from statements he made over the weekend suggesting an agreement to end the war with Iran was close. Trump held to what were described as maximum demands on Iran during the meeting.

The incident in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil shipments, targeted a commercial vessel. US forces intervened to eliminate the threat posed by the Iranian drones to shipping traffic in the strategic passage.

The timing of the military action complicates ongoing diplomatic efforts. The US and Iran have been engaged in talks aimed at resolving the conflict, but Wednesday's exchange of fire underscores the fragility of the negotiation process.

US Central Command confirmed its forces conducted the operation in response to the immediate threat. The command said the action was taken to protect commercial shipping and maintain freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-fifth of global oil consumption passes.

cards.headline: DOJ opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: The Justice Department has launched a criminal probe into whether Carroll committed perjury during a deposition.
cards.body:
Original Card (Unchanged)

The Department of Justice has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to multiple reports. CNN first reported the development Wednesday night.

The DOJ probe focuses on whether Carroll committed perjury while speaking at a deposition as part of her two civil cases against Trump. Carroll previously won two civil verdicts against the president in cases related to her sexual assault allegations and subsequent defamation claims.

---

Note: I'm returning the original card unchanged because the source material confirms the same core facts already present in your original text. The sources add minor detail (Carroll's age, the 2022 timing of the deposition, her statement about not accepting outside financial support) but don't materially alter the story's substance or require a rewrite.

cards.headline: Former judges ask court to probe Trump IRS settlement
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former federal judges wants a court to reopen Trump's lawsuit against the IRS over a $1.776 billion settlement fund.
cards.body:
A bipartisan group of former federal judges filed a request on Wednesday to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. They argue the administration bypassed proper judicial oversight by negotiating a settlement rather than allowing the court to resolve the case.

The settlement established a $1.776 billion fund intended to compensate those who claim government wrongdoing. The former judges contend this arrangement circumvented necessary court supervision of the dispute between Trump and the IRS.

cards.headline: Appeals court allows pro-Palestinian activist to remain free pending Supreme Court appeal
cards.teaser: A federal appeals panel ruled that Mahmoud Khalil can stay out of custody while he petitions the Supreme Court.
cards.body:
A federal appeals court panel allowed pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil to remain free on Tuesday as he pursues his case against the Trump administration at the Supreme Court. The three-judge panel included jurists appointed by Presidents Trump, George W. Bush, and Joe Biden.

Judges Stephanos Bibas, Arianna Freeman, and Thomas Hardiman issued the order keeping Khalil out of custody while he advances his Supreme Court petition.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans endorse Paxton after primary win over Cornyn
cards.teaser: Senate leadership is working to unify the party behind Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following his costly primary victory.
cards.body:
Senate Republican leaders are working to mend relationships with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and signal support from major donors as they seek to maintain their majority. Senate Majority Leader John Thune spoke with Paxton by phone on Wednesday before endorsing him on a radio show.

The effort follows a $130 million Senate primary in which Paxton defeated Senator John Cornyn. Republican leaders want to move past the contentious primary battle and focus on the general election against the Democratic nominee.

cards.headline: Zelensky asks Trump and Congress for Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: The Ukrainian president urged US leaders to supply air defense systems to help end the conflict with Russia.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged President Trump and members of Congress on Wednesday to supply Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors. He said the systems would help end Ukraine's conflict with Russia.

Zelensky said Ukraine has succeeded in defending against drones but has not built its own capability to produce anti-missile defense systems. He made the appeal directly to US leadership for the advanced air defense technology.
